project.name: EU merchant onboarding (KYB)
project.description: A payments company onboards merchants across the EU. Regulation is heavy and also evolving (new EU AML rules), and the product team ships often. Good for showing a hybrid recommendation.

documents.title: 01 Sales Head Interview
documents.masked_text:
Interview with Lukas Weber (Head of Sales)

We lose merchants because onboarding takes days. Competitors approve small merchants in under an hour. I want automated approval for low-risk merchants within one hour and a human only for the rest. We release product changes every two weeks and want onboarding to keep up with that pace.

Merchants should upload their company registration and the IDs of the owners from a web portal, and they should be able to see where they are in the process. Sales also needs a dashboard of applications stuck in review.

documents.title: 02 Mlro Memo
documents.masked_text:
Memo from Elena Costa, MLRO. Subject: Merchant due diligence

Every merchant must be screened against EU and UN sanctions lists at onboarding and daily afterwards. We must identify every beneficial owner holding more than 25 percent or exercising control, and verify them. Politically exposed persons need MLRO approval before activation. Merchants from high-risk third countries need enhanced due diligence.

Automated rejection of a merchant must be reviewable by a human on request. All onboarding records are kept for five years after the relationship ends. The new EU AML regulation applies from 2027 and will change several of these rules, so thresholds and checks must be configurable rather than hard-coded. Suspicious activity must be reportable to the financial intelligence unit without alerting the merchant.

documents.title: 03 Platform Team Notes
documents.masked_text:
Platform engineering notes (Sven Larsen)

- We deploy continuously to production with automated tests and security scans. Onboarding should use the same pipeline.
- Document checks and screening will use external vendors through APIs. Vendor outages must not lose applications.
- Personal data of beneficial owners is processed under GDPR. A data protection impact assessment is needed because we process identity documents at scale.
- The service must handle 500 onboarding applications per hour at peak with 99.9 percent availability.
- Every decision and every access to identity documents must be logged for audit.

controls.title: Customer identification and verification
controls.description: Regulated entities must identify every customer before establishing an account-based relationship and verify identity using an Officially Valid Document (passport, driving licence, voter ID, proof of Aadhaar possession, NREGA card) or its equivalent e-document, together with PAN or Form 60. Customers must not be allowed to open anonymous or fictitious-name accounts.

controls.title: Risk-based customer categorisation
controls.description: Each customer must be categorised as low, medium or high risk using documented parameters such as customer type, geography, product, delivery channel and transaction pattern. The intensity of due diligence and monitoring must match the assigned risk category, and the categorisation must be reviewable.
controls.suggested_requirement: The system shall assign every customer a documented low, medium or high risk category at onboarding and re-assess it when customer information or behaviour changes.

controls.title: Sanctions and watchlist screening
controls.description: Customers and related parties must be screened against applicable sanctions lists, and assets of designated persons must be frozen without delay and reported to the authorities.

controls.title: PEP identification and senior approval
controls.description: Institutions need risk-management systems to determine whether a customer or beneficial owner is a politically exposed person and, for foreign PEPs and higher-risk domestic PEPs, must obtain senior management approval, establish source of wealth and funds, and conduct enhanced ongoing monitoring.

controls.title: Beneficial ownership of legal entities
controls.description: For companies, partnerships, trusts and other legal entities, the natural persons who ultimately own or control the entity must be identified and verified. A controlling ownership interest is defined by a percentage threshold set in the direction (verify the current figure); where no owner meets the threshold the person exercising control, or the senior managing official, is identified.

controls.title: Enhanced due diligence for high-risk customers
controls.description: High-risk customers, politically exposed persons and non-face-to-face customers require enhanced due diligence: additional identity evidence, source of funds or wealth where relevant, senior management approval before establishing or continuing a relationship with a PEP, and closer ongoing monitoring.

controls.title: Notice and consent for personal data
controls.description: Personal data may be processed only for a lawful purpose, with free, specific, informed and unambiguous consent after a clear notice, or under a defined legitimate use such as compliance with a legal obligation. Consent must be as easy to withdraw as to give, and the data fiduciary must be able to show it was obtained.

controls.title: Data minimisation and purpose limitation
controls.description: Only the personal data necessary for the stated purpose may be collected, and it must be erased once the purpose is served unless a law requires retention. KYC records retained under anti-money-laundering law are a legal-retention case.
controls.suggested_requirement: The system shall collect only the identity data necessary for KYC and shall not reuse it for other purposes without separate consent.

controls.title: Record retention for at least five years
controls.description: Identification records and transaction records must be preserved for at least five years after the business relationship ends or the transaction takes place, in a form that can be produced promptly for competent authorities.

controls.title: Ongoing transaction monitoring
controls.description: Transactions must be monitored on an ongoing basis against the customer's profile and risk category, with alert rules calibrated to risk, documented alert handling, and prescribed threshold reports such as large cash transactions.

controls.title: Suspicious activity reporting
controls.description: Reporting entities must report suspicious transactions to the Financial Intelligence Unit - India promptly after concluding that a transaction is suspicious (the Rules set a short working-day deadline, verify the current figure), must not tip off the customer, and must keep the reasoning for decisions not to report.

controls.title: Biometric liveness and presentation-attack detection
controls.description: Biometric capture used for identity verification should include presentation attack detection (liveness) that is tested against spoofing with photos, replayed video, masks and deepfakes, and report attack-detection error rates.

controls.title: Document authenticity and tamper detection
controls.description: Identity assurance level 2 requires evidence of identity to be validated as genuine and the applicant to be verified as its owner, in person or remotely, using biometric comparison or equivalent, with detection of forged or tampered documents and presentation attacks.

controls.title: Tamper-evident audit trail of KYC decisions
controls.description: Identification records and transaction records must be preserved for at least five years after the business relationship ends or the transaction takes place, in a form that can be produced promptly for competent authorities.

controls.title: Encryption and masking of KYC data
controls.description: The data fiduciary must protect personal data in its possession or under its control, including data processed by processors, by taking reasonable security safeguards such as encryption, obfuscation or masking, access controls and logging, to prevent a personal data breach.

controls.title: Role-based access to KYC data
controls.description: An information security management system should apply controls for access management and least privilege, cryptography, logging and monitoring, secure development, supplier relationships and incident management.
controls.suggested_requirement: The system shall restrict access to KYC records by role on a least-privilege basis and log every access to full identity documents.

controls.title: Breach detection and notification
controls.description: On a personal data breach the data fiduciary must notify the Data Protection Board and each affected data principal in the prescribed form and manner.

controls.title: Data-subject rights handling
controls.description: Data principals have the right to access a summary of their data and processing, to correct and complete it, to request erasure (subject to legal retention), to grievance redress, and to nominate another person to exercise rights.

controls.title: Manual review and appeal of automated decisions
controls.description: People have the right not to be subject to solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects, such as automatically rejecting an account application. Where such decisions are permitted, safeguards include the right to human intervention, to express a view and to contest the decision.

threats.threat: Submission of forged identity documents or deepfake media by malicious actors.
Unauthorized modification of screening thresholds to bypass sanctions checks.
Human reviewer denies performing a specific approval or rejection action.
Unauthorized access to PII by internal staff exceeding their role-based permissions.
Overloading the document upload portal to prevent legitimate merchant onboarding.
Exploiting the CI/CD pipeline to gain administrative access to the production KYC environment.
Leaking of identity documents during transit between the system and external screening vendors.
Manipulation of application status tracking to deceive merchants about the review process.

risks.risk: Vague definition of 'low-risk' leads to inconsistent automated approvals, potentially onboarding high-risk entities.
risks.mitigation: Define specific, quantifiable risk scoring criteria for automated approval.

risks.risk: Lack of clear routing criteria results in operational bottlenecks or missed high-risk reviews.
risks.mitigation: Establish a documented decision matrix for human intervention triggers.

risks.risk: Two-week release cycle may be too slow to respond to urgent regulatory changes or critical security patches.
risks.mitigation: Implement an emergency hotfix process outside the standard release cycle.

risks.risk: Insecure document upload portal could lead to unauthorized data access or malicious file injection.
risks.mitigation: Implement strict file type validation, malware scanning, and secure storage.

risks.risk: Improper handling of sensitive UBO identity documents leads to GDPR violations and data breaches.
risks.mitigation: Apply encryption at rest and strict access controls to UBO data.

risks.risk: Lack of transparency in status tracking may lead to customer frustration and increased support overhead.
risks.mitigation: Define clear status states and automated notifications for applicants.

risks.risk: Inadequate visibility into stuck applications causes regulatory delays in onboarding timelines.
risks.mitigation: Implement automated alerts for applications exceeding defined SLA thresholds.

risks.risk: Failure to screen against sanctions lists results in severe regulatory fines and legal liability.
risks.mitigation: Implement automated, real-time screening against global sanctions databases.

risks.risk: Failure to perform daily screening allows sanctioned entities to continue using services undetected.
risks.mitigation: Schedule automated daily batch processing for all active merchant profiles.

risks.risk: Inaccurate UBO identification leads to non-compliance with AML directives and potential money laundering.
risks.mitigation: Integrate with official business registries for automated UBO verification.

risks.risk: Failure to verify UBOs allows shell companies to bypass KYC controls.
risks.mitigation: Mandate identity document verification for all identified beneficial owners.

risks.risk: Ambiguous PEP approval process leads to unauthorized onboarding of high-risk individuals.
risks.mitigation: Define a mandatory, documented MLRO sign-off workflow for all PEPs.

risks.risk: Incomplete EDD procedures for high-risk countries increase exposure to financial crime.
risks.mitigation: Implement a mandatory EDD checklist for all merchants from high-risk jurisdictions.

risks.risk: Lack of a clear appeals process for automated rejections may lead to regulatory complaints and loss of business.
risks.mitigation: Provide a clear, documented path for manual review requests.

risks.risk: Premature deletion of records leads to inability to provide evidence during regulatory audits.
risks.mitigation: Implement automated retention policies with legal hold overrides.

risks.risk: Hardcoded thresholds prevent rapid response to changing risk appetites or regulatory requirements.
risks.mitigation: Develop a secure configuration management interface for risk parameters.

risks.risk: Accidental disclosure of suspicious activity reports (SARs) to the merchant constitutes 'tipping off', a criminal offense.
risks.mitigation: Restrict access to SAR reporting tools to authorized compliance staff only.

risks.risk: Incompatible deployment pipelines could lead to failed updates or system instability.
risks.mitigation: Perform a technical audit of the CI/CD pipeline against KYC system requirements.

risks.risk: Unreliable API integrations lead to system downtime and failure to perform mandatory checks.
risks.mitigation: Implement robust error handling and circuit breakers for all external API calls.

risks.risk: Data loss during vendor outages results in incomplete KYC records and compliance gaps.
risks.mitigation: Implement a persistent message queue to retry failed vendor requests.

risks.risk: Non-compliant data processing leads to severe GDPR fines and loss of customer trust.
risks.mitigation: Conduct a comprehensive data mapping and privacy impact assessment.

risks.risk: Failure to perform a DPIA leaves the organization vulnerable to regulatory scrutiny and privacy risks.
risks.mitigation: Mandate a DPIA as a prerequisite for system deployment.

risks.risk: System failure during peak load leads to business disruption and potential loss of revenue.
risks.mitigation: Conduct load testing to validate capacity against the 500/hr requirement.

risks.risk: Unplanned downtime prevents critical KYC checks, halting business operations.
risks.mitigation: Implement high-availability architecture with redundant components.

risks.risk: Insufficient audit logs prevent reconstruction of decisions, leading to audit failure.
risks.mitigation: Implement centralized, immutable logging for all system decisions.

risks.risk: Unauthorized access to identity documents goes undetected without granular access logs.
risks.mitigation: Implement detailed audit trails for all document access events.

risks.risk: Failure to obtain valid consent leads to illegal data processing and regulatory penalties.
risks.mitigation: Implement a mandatory, timestamped consent capture mechanism in the UI.

risks.risk: Weak identity verification allows fraudulent actors to bypass onboarding controls.
risks.mitigation: Use certified liveness detection and biometric matching vendors.

risks.risk: Data exposure due to lack of encryption leads to massive data breach and regulatory fines.
risks.mitigation: Enforce AES-256 encryption at rest and TLS 1.3 in transit.

risks.risk: Excessive user privileges lead to internal data theft or unauthorized document access.
risks.mitigation: Implement Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) and regular access reviews.

risks.risk: Delayed incident notification leads to increased regulatory penalties under GDPR.
risks.mitigation: Establish and test an incident response plan with clear notification timelines.

risks.risk: Inability to fulfill data subject requests leads to non-compliance with GDPR rights.
risks.mitigation: Develop automated workflows for data access and erasure requests.

risks.risk: Tampered documents accepted as valid, leading to successful identity fraud.
risks.mitigation: Use automated document forensic analysis tools.

risks.risk: Compromised API tokens allow attackers to intercept or manipulate verification data.
risks.mitigation: Enforce short-lived tokens and secure secret management.

risks.risk: Malicious files uploaded to the system compromise internal infrastructure.
risks.mitigation: Integrate automated malware scanning into the file upload pipeline.

risks.risk: Unauthorized modification of screening thresholds allows high-risk entities to bypass controls.
risks.mitigation: Implement multi-party authorization for all configuration changes.

risks.risk: Failure to purge data leads to excessive data retention, violating GDPR minimization principles.
risks.mitigation: Automate data lifecycle management with verified deletion logs.

risks.risk: Credential theft leads to unauthorized access to sensitive KYC data.
risks.mitigation: Mandate phishing-resistant MFA for all internal users.

risks.risk: Lack of integrity in decision logs allows for tampering with audit trails.
risks.mitigation: Use digital signatures for all decision logs to ensure non-repudiation.

risks.risk: Brute-force attacks on upload endpoints lead to service degradation or data scraping.
risks.mitigation: Implement rate limiting and IP-based blocking at the WAF level.

narrative.explanation: The Agile-V hybrid model is the best fit because it balances the need for structured, traceable documentation required by the high regulatory criticality (4/5) and security risks (3/5) with the flexibility needed for vague requirements (3/5 stability). While the project faces significant legacy integration dependencies (4/5), the hybrid approach allows for iterative development cycles that accommodate the 77% vague requirement rate. The runner-up, Agile-DevSecOps, offers stronger continuous deployment capabilities but may lack the formal verification rigor necessary for your specific audit and compliance demands.
tradeoffs: Increased overhead due to maintaining both agile velocity and formal V-model documentation.
Potential friction between rapid development cycles and the need for rigorous regulatory sign-offs.
Complexity in managing synchronization points between the agile development team and the verification team.
would_change_if: If regulatory requirements are finalized and documentation demands decrease, a pure Agile-DevSecOps model would become more efficient.
If legacy system integration proves more volatile than expected, a shift toward a more rigid Waterfall model may be required to ensure system stability.
